newsitem.title: USA: Before killing, accused man drank, had tryst.
newsitem.headline: Before killing, accused man drank, had tryst.

text.p: Accused murderer Jonathan Schmitz had several drinks during a romantic tryst the night before he gunned down a gay man who had revealed a crush on him on national television, the woman who was with him said on Friday.

Michelle Wright told prosecutors she did not notice anything unusual about Schmitz when he was at her house the night before the killing. They drank, kissed and then moved off to sleep in separate rooms, she said.

Wright, who had worked with Schmitz as a waiter at the Fox & Hounds restaurant in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan, exchanged several smiles with the defendant and also broke down in tears during her testimony.

Schmitz is charged with shooting Scott Amedure to death three days after appearing on the "Jenny Jones" TV talk show. He said he was humiliated by Amedure having expressed his homosexual crush on him on a taping of the national TV show.
Schmitz, 26, who says he is heterosexual, claims he was suffering from manic depression and Graves disease, a thyroid condition with emotional side-effects, at the time he shot Amedure, 32.

Prosecutors in Oakland County Circuit Court have charged Schmitz with first-degree murder. They allege he knew what he was doing the morning of March 9, 1995, when he purchased a shotgun and shells, drove to Amedure's mobile home in Orion Township, Michigan, and fired two blasts into his chest.
However, one prosecution witness played into the defence strategy that Schmitz was ill at the time of the killing.

"I think anybody that murders somebody, there's something wrong with them," Donna Riley said under cross examination. Riley, a friend of Schmitz and Scott Amedure, appeared on the Jenny Jones show with them.
During a recess, Scott Amedure's brother Frank confronted defence attorney James Burdick, demanding to know how the events on the TV show were an excuse for his brother's murder.
"If I spit in your face on national television, that doesn't justify you killing me," he told Burdick.
Speaking later to reporters, Amedure said his brother and Riley did not set out to embarrass or hurt Schmitz. "It was all intended as friends."
On Monday, the trial will resume with testimony from Wright. Jurors will also hear from Gary Brady, Scott Amedure's roommate, who witnessed the shooting.

The jury will have the option of convicting Schmitz of first- or second-degree murder, manslaughter, or reckless discharge causing death. The first-degree murder charge carries a penalty of life without possibility of parole.
